explanations.answer: Rebuilds them and settles Israelites there
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. Solomon, David's son and Israel's king, rebuilds the cities Hiram had given him and settles Israelites there (2 Chronicles 8:2). Somebody handed him a fixer-upper and he said, "I got this." I got a drawer once and all I did was lie in it.

explanations.answer: Hands them back to Hiram as a gift
explanations.explanation: Nice thought, friend, but the text goes another way. Solomon doesn't hand anything back. He rebuilds the cities Hiram had given him and settles Israelites there (2 Chronicles 8:2). Hiram was king of Tyre, and these cities stay in Solomon's hands.

explanations.answer: Leaves them empty and falling apart
explanations.explanation: Not these cities, friend. Solomon rebuilds them and settles Israelites there (2 Chronicles 8:2). Empty and falling apart sounds like my old drawer, and that's NOT where this story goes.
True, baker. The text says Solomon went to Hamath-zobah and captured it (2 Chronicles 8:3). Short verse, big result. No speech, no fuss, just done.
Close, but the text says it plainly. Solomon went to Hamath-zobah and captured it (2 Chronicles 8:3). So the answer is True. Solomon, David's son and Israel's king, doesn't just show up and wave.

Right, baker. The text says Solomon conscripted these people to be forced laborers, as they are to this day (2 Chronicles 8:8). These were descendants who remained in the land, and the Israelites had not destroyed them. It's a heavy part of the passage, and I think it's worth slowing down on.

explanations.answer: Sends them out of the land
explanations.explanation: Not quite, friend. The text says these descendants remained in the land, and Solomon conscripted them to be forced laborers (2 Chronicles 8:8). Nobody is sent out. This is a heavy part of the story, so I'll say it plainly.

explanations.answer: Gives them land of their own
explanations.explanation: That's not what the text says, baker. Solomon conscripted these people to be forced laborers, as they are to this day (2 Chronicles 8:8). No land is handed over. It's a heavy verse, and I think it hurts a little to read.

explanations.answer: His men of war and commanders
explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. Solomon didn't consign any Israelites to slave labor, because they were his men of war, the leaders of his captains, and the commanders of his chariots and cavalry (2 Chronicles 8:9). That's a whole army with a whole chain of command. Plenty of folks with titles.

Good guess, since this whole passage is about building, but no. The text says the Israelites were his men of war, the leaders of his captains, and the commanders of his chariots and cavalry (2 Chronicles 8:9). Solomon didn't consign any of them to slave labor. The building crews aren't how the text describes them.

Not this time, friend. The text says the Israelites were his men of war, the leaders of his captains, and the commanders of his chariots and cavalry (2 Chronicles 8:9). Farming and shepherding don't come up in this verse. This is a military lineup.

explanations.answer: The places the ark has entered are holy
explanations.explanation: You got it, baker. Solomon says, "My wife must not live in the house of David king of Israel, because the places the ark of the LORD has entered are holy." (2 Chronicles 8:11) That's the reason the text gives, and it's the one Solomon gives. So he moves her to the palace he built for her.

explanations.answer: The house of David belongs to the priests
explanations.explanation: Good try, friend, but the text never says that. Solomon says, "My wife must not live in the house of David king of Israel, because the places the ark of the LORD has entered are holy." (2 Chronicles 8:11) The reason is about holy places, not who owns the house.

explanations.answer: The house of David is too small for her
explanations.explanation: Ha, nope, no size complaints in this text. Solomon says, "My wife must not live in the house of David king of Israel, because the places the ark of the LORD has entered are holy." (2 Chronicles 8:11) Holiness is the reason, not square footage.

Careful, baker, this one is tricky. The text says Solomon acted "in keeping with the ordinances of his father David," and the gatekeepers were appointed because it had been the command of David, the man of God (2 Chronicles 8:14). So it's False. Solomon wasn't making up a brand new plan.

That's right, baker. Solomon appointed the divisions of the priests and the Levites "in keeping with the ordinances of his father David," and the gatekeepers were set up because it had been the command of David, the man of God (2 Chronicles 8:14). So this wasn't a plan apart from David. Solomon, David's son, was carrying out what his father commanded.

explanations.answer: Without turning aside in any matter
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. The text says they "did not turn aside from the king's command regarding the priests or the Levites in any matter, including that of the treasuries." (2 Chronicles 8:15) Any matter, and that includes the treasuries. That's a crew that follows instructions.

explanations.answer: In every matter except the treasuries
explanations.explanation: Almost, but that's flipped. The text says they did not turn aside from the king's command "in any matter, including that of the treasuries." (2 Chronicles 8:15) The treasuries are part of it, not the exception.

explanations.answer: Only in matters on the feast days
explanations.explanation: Not quite, friend. The text says they did not turn aside from the king's command regarding the priests or the Levites "in any matter" (2 Chronicles 8:15). It isn't limited to feast days. It covers everything, even the treasuries.

True, baker. The text says all the work of Solomon was carried out, from the day the foundation was laid for the house of the LORD until it was finished (2 Chronicles 8:16). So the house of the LORD was completed. Start to finish, nothing left hanging.

Not this time, friend. The text says all the work of Solomon was carried out, from the day the foundation was laid until it was finished, and the house of the LORD was completed (2 Chronicles 8:16). So the answer is True. It got done.

That's him, baker. Hiram sent Solomon ships captained by his servants, along with crews of experienced sailors (2 Chronicles 8:18). Hiram is the same king of Tyre who gave Solomon those cities (2 Chronicles 2:3). Looks like he's a generous neighbor.

Pharaoh's daughter is Solomon's wife in this passage (2 Chronicles 8:11), so I see why he came to mind. But the ships and sailors come from Hiram, king of Tyre (2 Chronicles 8:18). Pharaoh isn't sending any boats here.

She doesn't show up in this passage, friend. The text says Hiram sent Solomon ships captained by his servants, along with crews of experienced sailors (2 Chronicles 8:18). Hiram is the king of Tyre who also gave Solomon cities.

Yes, baker. They went to Ophir and acquired 450 talents of gold, which they delivered to King Solomon (2 Chronicles 8:18). A talent is a big weight, so that's a LOT of gold. Hiram's sailors were experienced, and it shows.
Cedar does come up in Solomon's story, but not here. The text says they went to Ophir and acquired 450 talents of gold (2 Chronicles 8:18). So the blank is gold.

Horses are in this passage, since Solomon has cities for his chariots and horses (2 Chronicles 8:6). But the ships to Ophir didn't bring back horses. They acquired 450 talents of gold and delivered it to King Solomon (2 Chronicles 8:18).
